# dsh-multi-chat

**Side-by-side sessions for the DeepSeek Harness web GUI, as an equal-cell grid.**
Click a session i

n the left sidebar and it joins the conversation area as its own pane: one
click → one session, thre

e clicks → three sessions. At most **three panes per row**; the grid
degrades to two or one column w

hen the window is narrow. The session you clicked (the shell's
current session) stays highlighted, e

very pane keeps its own bottom-pinned input box, and panes
can be reordered by dragging the **⠿ hand
le in the top-right corner** of a pane header.

中文说明：README.zh.md · 设计依据：docs/design.md ·
Design notes (EN): docs/design.en.md
## What it does
| **Follow the sidebar** | Every session you click in the sidebar becomes a pane. The pane order sur

vives a page reload. |
| **Equal-cell grid** | At most three equal cells per row (`3 × 3` = 9 panes
max, six by default). Rows share the height but never below a comfortable pane height (~420 px); bey

ond that the grid scrolls. Narrow windows degrade 3 → 2 → 1 columns. |
| **Highlight** | The current

session's pane is ringed, its title emphasized, and its sequence badge inverts. |
| **Focus by clic
k** | Clicking inside a non-active pane asks the shell to make that session current (the official si

debar highlight follows). |
| **Reorder by drag** | Grab the ⠿ handle at the top-right of a pane hea
der (immediate drag) or press the header itself (4 px of travel, or a 300 ms hold on touch). Drop on
another pane to **swap** the two, drop on empty grid space to move the pane to the end, `Esc` cance

ls. The dragged pane follows the pointer as a ghost card and the drop target is outlined. |
| **Reor
der by keyboard** | The handle is focusable: `Ctrl/⌘ + arrows` swaps with the neighbouring cell (gri

d-aware for up/down), otherwise nothing happens. |
| **Close** | Each pane has a close control. The
active pane can only be closed by handing the shell over to a sibling — otherwise the control is dis

abled with a reason. The toolbar's **Keep only active** collapses the grid. |
| **Sidebar toggle** |
Each session row gets an extra action button (next to archive/pin) that adds/removes that session a

s a pane **without** navigating. |
| **Degrade, never break** | A single pane → the official single-
session UI is used untouched. Unknown/closed sessions render a note card. A crashed pane is containe
d by a pane-level error boundary. No `slots`/`sessions` service → the plugin stays inert instead of
failing the web boot. |
## Diagnostics
If switching sessions still shows only one pane, enable the opt-in browser log in DevTools: `localSt
orage.setItem('dsh-multi-chat:debug', '1')`, then reload and reproduce. Filter the console for `[dsh
-multi-chat:debug]`. Events report counts, booleans, viewport width, and slot registration outcomes
only; they omit session ids and conversation content. Disable with `localStorage.removeItem('dsh-mul
ti-chat:debug')`. A running local Web profile can also be inspected with `node scripts/browser-diagn
ostics.mjs --port <port> --token <startup-token>`; this reports rendered grid/pane/button counts and
does not create or switch sessions.
## Install

The package is a DSH bundle plugin: the host half (`.` → `lib/index.js`) only exists so the
package

becomes a loader entry; the browser half (`./client` → `lib/client.js`) is what the web
shell loads
through the `dsh.client` declaration.

## Development
[代码示例省略，未执行]
**v0.3.0 feature — the grid can be switched off**: pick **Settings → Plugins → dsh-multi-chat** and

flip
*Enable the side-by-side grid* (or press **Exit grid** in the toolbar). Off returns the convers

ation area to
the official single-session view; the pane set is remembered. **Keep only active** is

different: it leaves the grid
enabled with one pane, so clicking another session adds a pane again.
The preference and pane set are stored separately.

**v0.2.6 fix**: the official turn navigator (the tick rail with turn previews on the right of a
conv

ersation) hid itself inside every pane, because the official stylesheet hides it whenever its
conver

sation container is narrower than 900px. One pane-scoped rule with higher specificity restores it

container is narrower than 900px. One pane-scoped rule with higher specificity restores it

## How it works (short version)

1. `ctx.sessions.list` is observed; the session with `retainedBy.mainView > 0` is the shell's
curren

t session. Each new current session joins an ordered pane set, which *is* the grid order.
2. Every p

ane holds its own `sessions.retain(id, { source: 'multichat' })` reference, so the
client keeps that

session's scope alive even after the user navigates away.
3. While 2+ panes are open the plugin reg

isters into the documented `main.conversation`
**replacement point** (`single` slot, lower `priority

`) and renders one
`<SessionProvider session={reference}>` subtree per pane around the official
`con

versation.content` Factory — rendered as **`variant: 'embedded'`**, which is what keeps
the composer

's phase-gated `position: sticky; bottom: 0` alive without the official
conversation root (see docs/

design.md §4.2). With one pane the registration
is disposed, restoring the official view.
4. Styles

use one tagged `<style>` element and only `--dsw-alias-*` / `--dsw-radius-*` theme
tokens, so light
and dark themes both work.
## Known limitations

- The official conversation header (title breadcrumbs, view tabs, header actions) belongs to the
ent

ry the plugin replaces and cannot be rendered by a third party, so grid mode draws its own
compact p

ane headers instead.
- Panes keep their sessions open, so N panes mean N live session streams; the d

efault ceiling is
six, and the hard cap is nine.
- Drag reordering is pointer-based (mouse/touch/pen

t boot path does not pass cordis config to browser plugins, so all knobs live in the
grid toolbar /
`localStorage` rather than in `cordis.patch.yml`.
